clue.text: On top of hill flog cow

definitions.note: used as a verb: to cow is to intimidate

parts.note: the brow is the summit or top of a hill
to flog someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: A farmer up on the hilltop whips a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' looks like the animal being flogged, but it is a verb meaning to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to bully or intimidate them into submission, which is the same idea.

clue.text: Epic film about adult such as Lady Audley

indicators.note: the epic-film letters go round, or about, the letter for adult

parts.note: an epic is something big in scale
a film is a thin layer, as a mist is
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A blockbuster movie made about a grown-up heroine from Victorian fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Audley, of the Victorian novel Lady Audley's Secret, hides a first marriage when she weds again. 'Epic film' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces that wrap A.
explanation.definitionFit: The secret of Lady Audley in Mary Elizabeth Braddon's novel is that she has married a second husband while her first still lives.

clue.text: Bloom somewhere in

definitions.meaning: a place in Florida, the answer to 7 down; the cross-reference number seems lost from the clue as held

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue almost certainly read 'Bloom somewhere in 7', pointing to FLORIDA at 7 down; the number has dropped out with the enumeration.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando Bloom is a Hollywood actor, and Orlando is also a city in central Florida, home of theme parks.

clue.text: Pioneers short holidays at Wembley?

parts.note: a break is a brief holiday, such as a weekend away
Wembley, the English national football stadium, was rebuilt and reopened in 2007, so it is a new ground

explanation.surface: Explorers take weekend trips to watch football at the national stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Wembley is London's national football stadium, demolished and rebuilt in the 2000s; the question mark flags that it is a whimsical description.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer is to do something no one has done before, the very sense of the idiom about innovating.

clue.text: A road in French forest

parts.note: en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: A road running through a woodland in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French forest' tempts a French wood, but 'in French' gives the pieces; the forest is the English one in Warwickshire, setting of As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forest of Arden is the ancient woodland of Warwickshire where Shakespeare set As You Like It.

clue.text: Intended to reach remote Scottish town

parts.note: a letter meant for someone is intended to reach them
remote means distant, far away

explanation.surface: A traveller aims to get to a far-flung town in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Forfar is a market town in Angus, in eastern Scotland.

clue.text: Uniquely, Connie and Alfie get excited before broadcast is over

indicators.note: the shuffled names come before the reversed word in the answer
excited letters are stirred up and rearranged, so the two names are shuffled together

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: turned over, the word for broadcast is read backwards

parts.note: to broadcast a signal is to emit it

explanation.surface: Connie and Alfie get carried away just before the programme ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get excited' shuffles CONNIE and ALFIE into ONCEINALIFE; 'broadcast' is EMIT and 'is over' turns it to TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done uniquely happens just one time, never to be repeated.

clue.text: Andy's missus free to visit a US state

parts.note: Flo is the wife of Andy Capp in the long-running British newspaper comic strip
to rid is to free, as in rid of pests

explanation.surface: A woman is at liberty to pay a call on an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Capp is a British cartoon character, a cloth-capped northern working man; his long-suffering wife is Flo.
explanation.definitionFit: Florida is the south-eastern American state, the peninsula between the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic.

clue.text: Feel aggrieved at accommodation charge round affluent part of England?

indicators.note: the word for the charge goes round the region's letters

parts.note: rent is what you pay for accommodation
SE, the South East, is the wealthy corner of England around London

explanation.surface: Tenants grumble about rents in the wealthy south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The South East of England, around London, is its richest region; the question mark admits the generalisation.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter or indignant about it.

clue.text: Translated Latin for 'smoother'

indicators.note: translated suggests changing a text's form, here the letters' order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A Latin text rendered into English as the word for smoother.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a dictionary entry; 'Translated' is the anagram signal on LATIN FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatiron is an old-fashioned iron heated on a stove and used to press clothes smooth.

clue.text: In Leeds I could go round in circles, wanting a bite to eat

indicators.note: letters going round in circles are spun about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A lost visitor in Leeds wanders round in circles, hungry for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is IN LEEDS I COULD GO, all fifteen letters; 'round in circles' shuffles them. 'wanting' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a popular variety of eating apple, something you might bite into as a snack.

clue.text: Little fellow's mostly mad with family

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: manic means wildly excited, mad
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A small man is described as rather crazy, like the rest of his relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A manikin is a dwarf or very small man.

clue.text: University into it, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters might be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A university is into it, perhaps: the business of teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: teaching is just what a university is into.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is teaching or instruction, the main business a university deals in.

clue.text: Contempt expressed in Speakers' Corner

indicators.note: expressed in hints that the word is held within the place name that follows

explanation.surface: Disdain is voiced at the famous open-air debating spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Speakers' Corner, in London's Hyde Park, is where anyone may stand up and speak; contempt is often voiced there, which helps the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn is open disdain or contempt for someone thought worthless.

clue.text: Redecorated most of apartment, using non-fade brown colour

indicators.note: something redecorated is done up differently, so the letters are rearranged
most of means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone redoes most of a flat in a lasting shade of brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last T from APARTMENT; 'Redecorated' rearranges APARTMEN. 'using' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A perma-tan is a suntan that seems never to fade, a lasting bronzed skin colour.

clue.text: Throws out plans

definitions.meaning: to throw something forward or outward, as a projector casts an image
schemes or undertakings being worked on

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means casts forward; as a plural noun it means planned schemes or undertakings.

clue.text: Introduction of new coins is a source of anxiety?

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: euros are the coins of the eurozone currency

explanation.surface: Bringing in the euro made people nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the anxious launch of the euro currency; the question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental disorder marked by anxiety, obsessions or phobias.

clue.text: Appear unhappy after final test

indicators.note: the word for unhappy comes after the word for appear

parts.note: to show up is to appear
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: Someone looks miserable after a final exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A showdown is a decisive confrontation that settles a contest once and for all.

clue.text: With endless suffering I study a musical instrument

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: hell is a state of great suffering
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Battling pain, I practise a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for study or memorise is an old word crosswords love.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicon is a large circular tuba worn around the player's body, used in marching bands.

clue.text: Announce topic for discussion

definitions.meaning: to put out or publish formally, as a statement

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to put out officially; as a noun it is a point in question being debated.

clue.text: Small portion of broth with corn? Recipe's unavailable

parts.note: broth is a thin soup

indicators.note: unavailable means that letter is missing from the word that comes before

parts.note: R, from the Latin recipe, is the abbreviation on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A recipe for corn soup lacks the instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for recipe, Latin for 'take', heading old prescriptions; corn without R gives CON.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupcon is a tiny amount, a mere hint or trace of something.

clue.text: Caught heading off and given a telling off

indicators.note: heading off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: trapped means caught

explanation.surface: A fugitive is caught heading away and is scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rapped is to be rebuked sharply, as with a rap over the knuckles.

clue.text: Free, in general

definitions.meaning: at liberty, as an escaped prisoner is
as a whole, as in the public generally

explanation.definitionFit: An escaped convict is described as not yet caught; the phrase also means as a whole, as in society generally.

clue.text: Inspector's reported a man on board

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is given as it sounds

parts.note: an inspector is a checker

explanation.surface: An inspector is said to be a man on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a crew member, but it is a draughts piece; the 's is short for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequer is a counter in the board game draughts, also called checkers in America.

clue.text: Music heard in church, sacred organ piece

indicators.note: a piece is a part, so the answer is a run of letters within the words

explanation.surface: Church music played as a sacred piece on the organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ piece' reads as a composition; 'piece' signals a part of 'sacred organ'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Creed, set to music as part of the Mass, is sung in church services.

clue.text: To get back on an even keel, learn set musical works

definitions.text: To get back on an even keel

parts.note: to pick up a skill is to learn it
the pieces, a set of particular compositions

explanation.surface: To recover your poise, learn some set pieces of music.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to recover and restore normal life after a disaster.

clue.text: Strip small room in house due for refurbishment

parts.note: a den is a small private room in a home

indicators.note: something up for refurbishment is to be done over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clear out a small room in a house that needs doing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To denude is to strip bare, removing a covering.

clue.text: Poet's written about you as people of note

indicators.note: the poet's name is written around the word for you

parts.note: John Donne is the poet; with the possessive his name gains S
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A poet writes about you, describing you as eminent people.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected or senior woman in a field.
